summary: The new focused PIT recipes delete the build-output report before Maven runs, but they can still leave an older archived report in the reusable evidence directory and later present it as current evidence.

findings.title: Focused PIT retry can retain stale archived XML
findings.trigger: Run the documented focused command successfully once, then rerun it with the same `EVID` directory and have Maven fail before producing `core/target/pit-reports/mutations.xml`.
findings.consequence: The old `$EVID/mutations.xml` remains in place. A later `process-metrics.py record --pit "$EVID"` can parse the previous run's mutation counts as evidence for the failed retry, contradicting the required inconclusive result.
findings.evidence: `mkdir -p` at verification/pit.md:66 deliberately reuses the evidence directory. The command deletes only `core/target/pit-reports/mutations.xml` at line 67. When the retry produces no source XML, the conditional at line 73 skips the copy but never removes an existing `$EVID/mutations.xml`; the generic recipe repeats the same sequence at lines 100-108. The delivery ledger explicitly permits passing the evidence directory to `--pit` at verification/delivery-ledger.md:46-50.
findings.suggestedFix: Before invoking Maven, create a unique evidence directory for each run or delete prior `$EVID/mutations.xml` and related evidence artifacts. Apply the same cleanup to both focused examples, and preserve a durable failure/inconclusive marker when no fresh XML is copied.
